text:
Justin Barron has been a first-round pick looking for a role for a while: drafted 25th overall by Colorado in 2020, then stops in Montreal and Nashville before St. Louis. This season the Blues are giving him one. He's playing 16:34 a night, up from 14:15, and he already has 9 points in 14 games, as many as he had in 52 games with the Predators last season.

So far the chances back it up. Over his last ten games he has 8 points where we'd expect about 3.6 at his ice time, and the quality of his own shots (expected goals, our measure of how dangerous a chance is) is up too. With him on the ice at five on five, St. Louis gets 55% of the expected goals, well above the team's share when he sits.

Now the caution. The Blues have scored 3.4 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there, and 14 games is a small sample. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged his exits last season: only 30% kept possession. If forecheckers start winning that battle, the minutes could slip. We'd watch whether he still plays 16-plus a night come December.
headline: Justin Barron is finally getting real minutes
